charts.title: what the shell is made of

charts.name: D
charts.title: pause, and the one live screen

A1.label: Main._ready main.gd:18 — switch_scene to the pre-instantiated menu

A2.label: Menu emits continue_requested or new_run_requested menu.gd:7

A4.label: Main.enter_map main.gd:41 — switch_scene to the pre-instantiated map

A5.label: Map._start_show map.gd:67 — persists pending_goal and node id, emits enter_game

A6.label: Main.enter_game main.gd:45 — instantiates a FRESH GameView every show

A7.label: Main.switch_scene main.gd:76 — add_sibling then remove_child. The old scene stays ALIVE and unfreed, which is why menu and map already keep their state

A8.label: Main.game_ended main.gd:53 — back to the map, queue_free the GameView and its Game child

B1.label: NEW Wall — Node2D, the whole app. QR1=a: nothing is ever drawn straight to the window again

B2.label: NEW Camera2D on the wall. The project's second camera; the map keeps its own inside its picture, Q31=a

B3.label: NEW WallLayout Resource — the authored PATTERN: ring slots, per-picture size multiplier Q16=c, per-picture frame thickness Q36, home picture Q9=a

B4.label: NEW Packer — pure function of layout plus unlocked set plus window aspect. Q21=a runtime, Q18=a strictly deterministic, Q20=a never overlapping

B5.label: NEW Picture — one per screen. A Sprite2D in wall space carrying a ViewportTexture. GAP-001=b: SubViewportContainer is documented as distorting when scaled, and the camera scales every picture continuously

B6.label: NEW Frame — one shared style parameterised by size and colour QR4=b. Thickness authored per picture and per side Q36 Q37=a, entirely outside the picture rect Q38=a, no mat Q39=a

B7.label: Screen — the existing scene, unchanged. Q211=a: no screen is redesigned, only reparented

B8.label: NEW Overlay — its own CanvasLayer Q202=a, so it does not ride the wall camera. Carries Back, Forward, Wall and the Info toggle per Q67 note and Q135 note

B9.label: NEW Profile — user://profile.tres beside settings, same ResourceSaver pattern Q152=a. Holds the unlocked set, keyed per save slot Q151=b

B10.label: Wall surface — a flat colour from the palette Q2=b, with per-picture drop shadows from one authored light position Q7=b and unlockable set dressing Q6=c

C1.label: A destination is requested — click Q88=a, keyboard Q99=a, controller, pinch Q119=a, or Back

C5.label: Input is ignored. Q56=b — no retargeting mid-flight

C6.label: NEW Build the destination screen NOW, synchronously, during the zoom-out. Q205=a places the cost under motion; Q206=b keeps the build one synchronous pass

C7.label: NEW One continuous tween. Q47=b: travel starts before the zoom-out ends and the zoom-in starts before the travel ends, so the camera arcs

C8.label: NEW Zoom out far enough to show BOTH frames. Q48=b — distance decides the zoom, so a far jump reads as a journey. TRANS_EXPO EASE_OUT, Q52=b

C9.label: NEW Source screen PAUSES the instant its frame's outer edge enters the view. Q72=a

C10.label: NEW Travel in a straight line across the wall. Q51=a. TRANS_SINE EASE_IN_OUT, Q53=b. Fixed duration regardless of distance, Q50=a

C11.label: NEW Destination UNPAUSES as soon as it is visible in the camera window at all. Q73=c — early, during the travel

C12.label: NEW Zoom in. TRANS_EXPO EASE_IN, Q52=b

C13.label: NEW Input unlocks BEFORE the tween ends — the moment the picture and its frame are fully in view. Q58 note

C14.label: NEW Landed. The picture overfills the window so no frame is visible at rest. Q176=a

C15.label: All durations are fractions of settings.base_delay. Q46=b — the wall paces with the game speed setting but never compresses like Game.get_delay does

C16.label: window resized mid-flight, retarget and continue Q26=a

C17.label: reduced motion replaces all of this with a cross-fade at a fixed zoom — chart K

D1.label: NEW get_tree().paused = true, held for the entire session. QR6=a

D2.label: NEW Wall, camera and overlay are PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, so the shell keeps running while everything else is stopped

D3.label: NEW Every screen root is PROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLE by default. QR6=a

D4.label: NEW The live screen's root is flipped to ALWAYS. Exactly one screen is ever ALWAYS

D5.label: Tweens need nothing — a tween made by node.create_tween is bound to its node and pauses with it

D6.label: NEW ESCAPE 1: SceneTree.create_timer defaults process_always = true and runs straight through the pause. One helper that passes false replaces every direct call. Q75=b

D7.label: NEW ESCAPE 2: shader TIME keeps advancing while paused. Accepted and hidden — a non-live picture is a frozen texture the whole time, so the jump can only land at unpause, under the zoom-in. Q222=c

D8.label: Wall view: NOTHING is live. Q74=a — no screen is ALWAYS while the wall is being looked at

D9.label: Info mode does NOT pause the focused screen. Q138=a — the pause rule keys off the transition, not off the zoom

D10.label: UNVERIFIED — whether a PAUSABLE material's TIME really stops is disputed. Check by eye before building on D7

D11.label: the board freezing mid-act — chart L

E2.label: Rendering runs normally at the screen's own design resolution. Q29=b, per-screen

E3.label: NEW SubViewport.render_target_update_mode = UPDATE_DISABLED. Q82=a — the texture persists, and that frozen last frame IS what the wall shows. QR8=b

E4.label: NEW At wall construction every picture is force-rendered ONCE so nothing is ever blank. Q78=b — costs one frame each at startup

E5.label: Wall-view resolution is SubViewport.size written directly, derived from the picture's on-screen pixel size. Q86=a, Q87=b, GAP-002 — one property, no manager, and any size rather than the integer divisor stretch_shrink would have given

E6.label: No render budget and no cap. Q85=b — frozen textures are cheap by construction

E7.label: NEW On window restore from minimise, every frozen texture is re-rendered; the GPU may have discarded them. Q208=b

E8.label: All screens stay instantiated for the whole session. Q203=a — nothing is ever torn down

E9.label: NEW Memory is instrumented anyway, behind the leak-sentinel debug gate. Q79 note, Q210=a — so the unload-to-placeholder fallback stays a measurement away

E10.label: A torn-down screen would write a state blob first. Q143=a — unreachable under Q203=a, kept as the contract if the cap ever arrives

F1.label: NEW Back stack of picture ids. Q63=a full history

F2.label: NEW Depth is bounded by the number of pictures. Revisiting a picture already in the stack MOVES it to the top rather than appending. Q64 note

F3.label: NEW A Forward button, so the picture you just left is one press away. Q64 note — a control the braindump did not have

F4.label: Wall view is NOT on the stack. Q66=b — it is only ever reached by the Wall button

F5.label: Back at the bottom of the stack goes to wall view. Q65=a

F6.label: Wall button toggles — press again to return where you were. Q68=a

F7.label: NEW Back, Forward, Wall and the Info toggle all live on the persistent overlay. Q67, Q135 — a top-right magnifying glass for Info, always accessible

F8.label: Back closes an open popup first; a second Back leaves the picture. Q164=a

F9.label: Wall button leaves the popup open behind it, still there on return. Q165=a

F10.label: NEW Each view keeps its OWN focus — the wall remembers its selected picture, and every picture remembers its internal focus for the session. Q107 note, Q58 note

F11.label: In wall view exactly one picture is selected, starting at the one you came from. Q69=a. Highlight is a frame glow plus a lift off the wall, shape and motion not colour. Q70=c, Q178=a

F12.label: Every picture is always enterable. Q71=c — no disabled pictures

G1.label: NEW Ellipse aspect follows the live window aspect, clamped to an authored min and max. Q10=c

G2.label: NEW Ring capacity is computed — as many as fit given picture sizes and the gap. Q11=b

G3.label: NEW Position within a ring is an authored slot index. Q12=a — the same on every player's wall, fixed art direction

G4.label: NEW A partial ring stays at its authored angles and reads as visibly unfinished. Q13=b

G5.label: NEW One uniform gap for the whole wall, measured between FRAME OUTER EDGES so uneven frame widths still space evenly. Q14=a, Q36 note

G6.label: Locked pictures are not drawn at all. Q158=a — no empty slots

G7.label: NEW On resize, both the ellipse and every picture's aspect change so a picture always matches the window shape. Q22=b

G8.label: Re-pack snaps instantly. Q25=a. Fullscreen toggle also snaps. Q28=b

G9.label: NEW Wall view FILLS the window, cropping the wall's long axis. Q5=b

G10.label: NEW Free pan is allowed ONLY when pictures fall outside the view; on a large screen everything is visible and panning is off. Q1 note, Q3 note. Never pans into void

G11.label: No free zoom in wall view — any zoom input is a request to enter a picture. Q4=b

G12.label: Pictures are square to the wall, no tilt, no parallax. Q15=a, Q8=a

G13.label: Floor is 1280x720. Q23 note. Aspect range 4:3 to 32:9. Q24=b

G14.label: a new unlock re-packs the wall — chart K

H1.label: Each screen has its OWN authored design resolution. Q29=b — the map is visually dense and gets more room than the deck viewer

H2.label: A picture's aspect need not be the window's. Q32=b — a square map picture and portrait pictures are allowed

H3.label: NEW At rest the focused picture OVERFILLS the window whenever its aspect does not match, so no frame is ever visible at rest. Q27 note, Q176=a

H4.label: NEW Every SubViewport sets canvas_item_default_texture_filter EXPLICITLY. A SubViewport defaults to LINEAR and does not inherit the project NEAREST — documented four times in this repo

H5.label: NEW The FOCUSED picture at rest samples NEAREST. Everything else — wall view, out of view, and any picture while the zoom is changing — samples LINEAR. Q34 note, QR7=c

H6.label: NEW The swap is driven by ZOOM change only. Pure translation stays as it is, so travelling does not flicker the filter. Q34 note

H7.label: A screen needing more room than its picture pans with its own internal camera. Q31=a — exactly what world_map_controller.gd does today

I1.label: NEW The wall routes input itself. An event over the focused picture is converted to the SubViewport's space with make_input_local against the sprite's transform, then handed over with SubViewport.push_input. GAP-001=b

I1b.label: NEW The screen's own Controls are untouched — they see ordinary events in their own viewport's coordinates, so no screen changes. This is what replaces the container doing it for us

I2.label: Non-focused pictures receive no input at all — the wall never pushes to them, and only its own picture-picking sees the event. Q95=a

I3.label: Mouse: click enters immediately Q88=a. The wheel always belongs to the focused screen Q89=a. Right-click does nothing Q91=b. Clicking bare wall does nothing Q93=a. Pointing cursor over an enterable picture Q97=a

I4.label: Keyboard: arrows move the selection SPATIALLY to the nearest picture in that direction Q98=a, wrapping Q106=a. ui_accept enters Q99=a. Number keys 1 to 9 jump directly Q104=a

I5.label: ui_cancel is Back, but the focused screen gets FIRST REFUSAL through _unhandled_input — a screen that uses Escape keeps it. Q100=a

I6.label: Tab is a new wall_overview action for wall view. Q101=a. All wall actions are ordinary rebindable InputMap actions. Q102=a

I7.label: Controller: left stick and d-pad both move the selection Q108=a, one step per press with a repeat after a hold delay Q116=a. Back is a shoulder button so B stays with the screens Q109=b. Wall is the Select or View button Q110=b. Always discrete, never a virtual cursor Q113=a

I8.label: Touch: fully supported, wall AND every screen Q118=a. Tap enters immediately Q120=a. Swipes belong to the screen Q121=a

I8b.label: NEW Pinch is derived BY HAND from InputEventScreenTouch and ScreenDrag — two tracked touch ids and a distance delta. GAP-003=a: InputEventMagnifyGesture never fires on Windows, which is where this is built and tested. A gesture addon is a later testing convenience, never a shipping dependency

I8c.label: NEW Touch targets are 9 mm from screen_get_dpi, CLAMPED to a pixel floor and ceiling. GAP-004=b: reported DPI is wrong on bad EDID, on multi-monitor Windows, and on Android, so the clamp is what makes the rule safe

I9.label: The wall never listens while a screen is focused, on any device. Q103=a, Q115=a

I10.label: The keyboard and controller cursor appears only after the first such input, so a mouse player never sees it. Q105=b. Most recent device wins and the other indicator hides. Q124=a

I11.label: One neutral icon per control, not per-device glyphs. Q125=b

I12.label: During a transition input is inert. Q96=a — until C13 unlocks it early

J1.label: A persistent toggle. Q127=a — a top-right magnifying glass on the overlay, always accessible, NOT persisted across sessions. Q135 note

J2.label: NEW Zooms out just enough to reveal the BOTTOM frame only. Top, left and right stay covered — deliberately not a full frame reveal. Q128 note

J3.label: NEW The notecard is anchored to the bottom of the WINDOW in screen space, over the wall. Q129=a

J4.label: NEW The notecard SIZES ITSELF to its contents, so each one reads as unique, and shows a copy of the hovered item as a visual beside the description. Q130 note

J5.label: NEW It shows nothing until something is hovered, then KEEPS showing the last card — so crossing empty space does not blink it in and out. Q131 note

J6.label: Leaving info mode resets it to nothing. Q131 note

J7.label: NEW Screens publish hoverables through a get_info interface. Q132=a, Q133=b

J8.label: NEW The existing tooltips MIGRATE to become the info card — map_hover_panel.gd and the board focus panel stop being separate systems. Q134=c

J9.label: Toggling mid-transition takes effect IMMEDIATELY, retargeting the camera. Q136=b

J10.label: With info mode on a transition is a pure travel — the camera never leaves the info zoom. Q137=a

J11.label: The focused screen stays LIVE at the info zoom. Q138=a

J12.label: Text size never shrinks. On a small screen or a long translation the card SCROLLS UPWARD over the whole picture, and must be scrolled back to see the picture again. Q140 note

K1.label: NEW Profile.unlock is called from game code; the condition lives wherever the feature does. Q153=a

K2.label: No reveal ceremony — the picture is simply there next time the wall is seen. Q154=c

K3.label: If the player is IN wall view when it happens, the re-pack animates live in front of them. Q155=a

K4.label: If they are inside a picture, the wall re-packs silently. Back still works because the stack holds ids, not positions. Q156=a

K5.label: NEW user://profile.tres, per save slot. Q152=a, Q151=b — even though only one slot exists today, Q213=a

K6.label: Wall state does NOT survive a quit. Every launch starts at the start menu, as main.gd:22 does now. Q145=b, Q149=a

K7.label: The run save gains no wall fields. Q150=a — wall state is profile-level

K8.label: NEW Reduced motion is a PlayerSettings flag that replaces every transition with a cross-fade at a fixed zoom. Q172=a. Its FIRST-LAUNCH default is read from DisplayServer.accessibility_should_reduce_animation, then it is an ordinary stored setting the moment the player touches it. GAP-005=a supersedes Q174=a. Falls back to OFF where the query is unavailable, and is UNVERIFIED on Windows

K9.label: Wall view still exists under reduced motion, reached by cross-fade. Q173=a

K10.label: There is no separate transition-speed knob — the always-instant setting IS the reduced-motion flag. Q175=b resolves Q59=c

K11.label: NEW A debug flag unlocks everything. Q159=a

L1.label: The board is an ordinary picture WITH a frame — the proscenium reading. Q189=a

L2.label: GameView is still built fresh per show and freed after, exactly as main.gd:45 and :53 do now. Q191 note

L3.label: NEW When there is no GameView the picture shows an authored default background image, which GameView may update. Q191 note

L4.label: Leaving mid-act FREEZES the act where it stands and resumes from the identical instant. Q186=d

L5.label: The guarantee covers everything the board owns — the coroutine chain, every tween, every timer, prop motion and the FX ease clocks. Bit-identical. Q221=a

L6.label: No moment refuses to freeze. Wall and Back are live at every instant of a show, including inside a modal choice. Q223=a

L7.label: Nothing announces a suspended act — the picture literally shows the board stopped mid-act. Q224=b

L8.label: A frozen act does NOT survive a quit. Mid-act state stays unpersisted, exactly as today. Q225=a

L9.label: Undo is unaffected — a frozen act completes on resume and is undoable as it would have been. Q226=a, Q190=a

L10.label: The spotlight dim stops at the frame. LightLayer stays the last sibling inside the screen; the wall never darkens. Q194=a, Q195=a

L11.label: FxAttachment._on_screen now culls against the SCREEN rect, and that is the correct answer with no code change. Q193=a

L12.label: After a lost run the map picture STAYS, showing its last state. Re-entering the game picture shows the game-over screen. The map is replaced only when a new run starts. Q157 note

L13.label: the two escapes from pause — chart D

M1.label: Cold launch: the camera starts already zoomed into the start-menu picture. It is an ordinary picture; there is simply nothing else on the wall yet. Q60=a

M2.label: Choosing a save triggers a one-off longer, slower zoom-out to wall view, distinct from an ordinary Wall press. Q61=a

M3.label: That reveal happens on EVERY launch. Q62=a

M4.label: Wall view is hidden entirely while only one picture exists. Q19=b

M5.label: NEW A tool scene beside Tools/fx_editor.tscn. Edits layout, slots, gaps, sizes AND per-picture frame parameters. Q179=c, QR5=a

M6.label: NEW It uses PLACEHOLDERS, with an option to swap in snapshots of the real scenes for colour comparison. Q180 note — a deliberate exception to the no-mocks rule, and the snapshot option is what keeps it honest

M7.label: Simulates window aspect Q181=a and unlock state Q182=a, and previews a transition with the real curves Q183=a

M8.label: Writes the same resource the game loads. Q185=a — so every script it touches must be @tool

M9.label: Never reads or writes profile data. Q200=a

M10.label: Per-picture music, cross-faded during transitions, with subtle distance attenuation and no new audio bus. Q167=c, Q170=b, Q171=b. A paused screen's audio fades out over the zoom-out Q168=c. Transitions themselves are silent Q169=c
